site.name: Sabbir
site.intro: I'm Sabbir — a video editor and motion designer turning raw footage into films that hold attention. Two years, fifty clients, and a stubborn obsession with the frame a cut lands on.
bio: I started in a small edit suite in Dhaka with a borrowed monitor and a stubborn belief that a cut can carry emotion better than a line of copy. Two years and fifty clients later, I still believe it — I've just gotten faster at proving it.

Today I work with brands, creators and studios on films, title sequences, product launches and social systems. My sweet spot is the overlap between editorial rhythm and motion design: pacing that makes a film breathe, and graphics that make a message land.
I care about the details most people never notice — the frame a cut lands on, the curve of an ease, the three frames of silence before the drop. That's where the work starts to feel expensive.

projects.title: Aether
projects.subtitle: Cinematic Brand Film
projects.summary: A 90-second manifesto film for a lighting brand — cut to breathe, graded to glow.
body: Aether builds architectural lighting, and their brief was simple: make light feel emotional. We shot for two nights across three locations, then cut a film that treats every fixture as a character rather than a product.

The edit runs on contrast — long, patient holds against two-frame hits. I graded warm ember into cool shadow so the product never competes with the mood, and layered a restrained optical-grain pass to keep it cinematic without looking vintage.
The final piece ran as the brand's site hero and their launch keynote opener. Watch-through beat their previous film by 38%.
Deliverables: 90s hero film, 30s and 15s cutdowns, 9:16 social edits, five silent loop backgrounds for the website.

projects.title: Nova Loop
projects.subtitle: Title Sequence
projects.summary: An opening title sequence built from concentric sound ripples and one stubborn circle.
body: Nova is a three-day electronic music festival. The identity was already a single ring; the challenge was making one shape feel like a night-long build-up.

I designed a title system where rings propagate like sound pressure, each beat spawning a new layer. Typography arrives late and leaves early — the sequence is 34 seconds and the logo owns only four of them.
Everything was built on a 12-frame rhythmic grid, so the whole sequence re-times cleanly to any track the festival uses.
Delivered as a ProRes 4444 master, an alpha overlay pack for the stage screens, and a set of reusable AE templates for their social team.

projects.title: Terra
projects.subtitle: Product Launch Film
projects.summary: A launch film where the product is a planet — macro texture, orbital light, no voiceover.
body: Terra's speaker is a sphere, and the team hated every 'product rotating on white' film they'd ever been pitched. So we built a world instead.

I modelled a simplified hero, lit it with a single orbital key, and matched it to macro plates of fabric and metal shot practically. The edit cross-cuts between scale extremes: a planet-wide horizon, then a two-centimetre stitch.
No voiceover, no feature list. Just sound design — a low sub that resolves exactly when the sphere turns. The brand's engineers sent me three messages about that pause.
Ran as the launch-day hero asset and the paid social lead, with nine aspect-ratio variants delivered from one timeline.

projects.title: Pulse
projects.subtitle: Social Campaign System
projects.summary: A 40-asset social system powered by one motion language and zero repetitive work.
body: Pulse needed 40 pieces of content a month without the output feeling templated. The answer was a motion language, not 40 animations.

I defined four moves — punch-in, whip-pan, speed-ramp, and a type wipe — and built them as re-usable AE and Premiere presets. Any editor on their team can now assemble a week of content in an afternoon and it still feels directed.
The first month outperformed their previous quarter on saves and shares; the system has since been extended to two regional accounts.
Included a typed asset kit, colour-grade LUT, caption styles and a 14-page usage guide.

projects.title: Monogram
projects.subtitle: Identity in Motion
projects.summary: Turning a static monogram into a 6-second signature that works at any scale.
body: Mono Atelier had a beautiful static mark and no idea how it moved. I built the motion identity around one idea: the letter draws itself the way ink behaves on paper — pressure first, then release.
The system includes a 6-second signature, a 1.5-second stinger, a loading loop and a set of transition wipes that all share the same easing curve.
Every asset was stress-tested from 120px favicons up to a 6-metre trade-show wall.
The brand book gained a 12-page motion appendix; the studio now uses the stinger in every client presentation.

projects.title: Horizon
projects.subtitle: Documentary Open
projects.summary: A 2-minute doc opener cut to silence, texture and a single moving horizon line.
body: Field Notes shot forty hours of coastal footage for a film about shifting shorelines. The opener had to establish scale without a narrator.
I cut against the sound of water rather than music — letting the ambience set the rhythm — and built a horizon line in motion that travels across every shot, tying the sequence together.
The title is set in a single weight and lands on a hard cut to black. Nothing else moves for two seconds. It's the moment people remember.
Delivered the full 74-minute documentary edit, the 2-minute opener, and a trailer for festival submissions.

projects.title: Bloom
projects.subtitle: Music Visualiser
projects.summary: A generative visualiser driven by the stems of a single track — no two loops identical.
body: Kaia wanted a visual for a track that builds for three minutes. Static loops wouldn't work, so I drove displacement directly from the song's stems.
Kick drives the scale pulse, hats drive grain, and the vocal stem controls a slow bloom. Because the input is audio, every render — and every live set — comes out slightly different.
Rendered at 4K in Cycles with a 3-hour budget, then composited and graded in After Effects for consistency across the section changes.
Now used as the official visualiser plus a live VJ pack with 24 clip variations.

projects.title: Dust
projects.subtitle: Fashion Film
projects.summary: A 45-second fashion film about garments in motion — cut on fabric, not on beats.
body: Ochre's collection was about weight and drape, so the film had to be edited on movement instead of music. Every cut lands when the fabric changes direction.
I spent a day in the grade building a warm, dusty palette with almost no blue — skin tones kept alive, shadows lifted just enough to keep the texture of the cloth.
The finished film runs in their showroom on loop and opened their Paris presentation.
Delivered 45s hero, three 10s product loops, and a print-safe stills pass pulled from the timeline.

services.title: Editing & Post
services.description: Story-first editing, colour and sound for brand films, documentaries and commercials. From rushes to delivery-ready master.

services.title: Motion & Titles
services.description: Title sequences, kinetic typography and motion systems that make a brand recognisable in half a second.

services.title: 3D & VFX
services.description: Product visualisation, compositing and generative motion. Built in Blender and finished in After Effects.

services.title: Creative Direction
services.description: The thinking before the timeline opens — concept, story structure, boards and a visual language the whole team can follow.

process.title: Brief & Discovery
process.description: A call, your references, and the uncomfortable questions. We agree on the feeling before we agree on the frames.

process.title: Concept & Boards
process.description: A treatment, a story structure and style frames. You see the film's skeleton before a single clip is cut.

process.title: Edit & Design
process.description: Two rounds of offline edit, motion built to the final timing, then a colour and sound pass.

process.title: Deliver & Systemise
process.description: Masters, cutdowns, captions and templates — delivered in an organised handover your team can actually use.
